High-level options (ballpark pricing below, will provide formal quote once you confirm option):

- Throughput: ~+38% aggregate throughput; expected p95 latency change: ~+15% improvement (depends on request mix)

Option B — Mid-term repackage and extend (add +8, extend term +12 months on new blended commit)

- We can offer tiered volume discounts (5–15%) depending on final commit size

Option C — Burst pool + autoscaling (no commit change)
- Reserve a small dedicated burst pool (4 nodes) + autoscale to customer pool when queued
- Cost: $ per-hour burst pricing plus small subscription — lower up-front but no commit discounts

Dylan — did a quick pass on the runbook and ran a small perf sim against their request mix (LLM batching patterns + avg seq length 512):

- Blended price: we do a weighted average across the remaining committed units and new nodes, then apply a volume discount tier. In this case: existing commit (40 nodes at current rate) + 8 new nodes blended over 12 months -> baseline blended price per node ~ $8,550. With a 10% volume-tier discount that they qualify for at this size, that moves to ~$7,695/mo per node effective.

- Throughput: adding +8 A100s in the same pool gives ~+36–40% aggregate throughput. Expected p95 latency improvement: ~12–18% depending on cache hit rates. p99 improvement is smaller (~8–10%).

- Migration risk: low if we add nodes as part of pool resize (no model snapshot required). Only caveat is KV cache warming for hot sessions — plan for a 48–72 hour warm-up to hit steady-state.

Recommendation: Offer Option B with a 10% discretionary discount and a $20k one-time migration credit (to cover any CS engineering hours and make procurement comfortable). That keeps net effective pricing in the mid-tier and preserves margin compared to a deeper per-node discount.

Attached: perf_summary.csv (summary), run_results.txt

—Karthik (SE)
